caption:
Your appraisal letter came with a bigger title and nothing behind it. Coverage in August 2026 put numbers to it: roughly 1 in 3 promoted Indian employees received no raise or under 5%, and around 57% of employers admit they hand out senior-sounding designations as a retention tactic.

Read that plainly. The designation was never the authority. It was the substitute for it.

In the military, command is not conferred by what is printed on a nameplate. It is established the moment you enter the room 
s Bearing before you speak. Tone that does not climb at the end of a sentence. Silence held long enough that the room turns to you to break it.

That is why your idea gets ignored until a louder voice repeats it. Not qualification. Not title. Presence.

A title someone else grants can be withdrawn. Command-authority you build in the room cannot.
alt_text: A plain dark card with bold white text reading: "A title someone else grants can be withdrawn. Command-authority you build in the room cannot." The Lumina Presence wordmark sits small at the bottom.

topic.title: The hollow promotion: title given, authority withheld
topic.angle: Lumina's audience are credentialled professionals who are still overlooked — title inflation is the institutional version of that exact wound, proving authority is established in the room through bearing, tone and calculated silence, not conferred by a designation.
topic.why_now: Indian coverage from 20 August 2026 surfaced survey data showing roughly 1 in 3 promoted Indian employees got no raise or under 5%, and ~57% of employers use senior-sounding designations as a retention tactic — landing just after a late-running 2026 appraisal cycle delivered appraisal letters, when the 'I got the title and nothing else' feeling is rawest.

rationale: A stark text-only visual carries the argument without visual metaphor, matching the caption's plainspoken authority and keeping the focus on the single hard line about conferred versus established authority.
